Key Insights for 2025

What the data tells us about where to invest right now.

📈

JVC Leads — But Watch Supply

JVC consistently delivers 8–9% gross yields, the highest in Dubai. However, with 12,000+ units under construction, supply pressure could compress yields by 2026. Lock in now or focus on Villa sub-communities.

🏖️

STR Beats LTR in Coastal Zones

Emaar Beachfront and Palm Jumeirah STR yields reach 8–12% (annualised at 75%+ occupancy) vs 4–5% LTR. Requires DTCM permit (AED 1,520/yr). Net advantage: ~2–3% higher returns for active managers.

🏡

Villas Outperforming Apartments

REIDIN data shows villa price growth at +15.16% vs apartments +12.52% YoY in 2025. However, apartment yields remain higher (7–9% vs 4–6% for villas). Villas = appreciation, apartments = income.

💰

Mortgage Math: Is It Covered?

At EIBOR + 1.5% (~4.99%), a 75% LTV mortgage on a AED 1.2M JVC apartment costs ~AED 5,200/month. Expected rent: ~AED 6,000/month. Monthly cashflow: +AED 800 before service charges.

🌊

Off-Plan Yields: The Hidden Risk

Off-plan properties show projected yields of 7–9% at current prices. But prices typically rise 15–25% by handover, compressing actual yield for buyers who miss the launch price. Buy at launch or in the secondary market.

🏆

Golden Visa Threshold: AED 2M

Properties ≥ AED 2M qualify for the 10-year UAE Golden Visa. This drives disproportionate demand at the AED 1.8–2.2M price band, supporting values and liquidity in communities like Dubai Hills and Downtown.

Frequently Asked Questions

What Dubai investors ask most about rental yields.

What is the average rental yield in Dubai in 2025?

The city-wide average gross rental yield in Dubai is approximately 6.9% in 2025, according to REIDIN and DLD data. This is significantly higher than London (3–4%), Singapore (3–4%), and New York (3–5%), making Dubai one of the highest-yielding major real estate markets globally.

Which area in Dubai has the highest rental yield?

Jumeirah Village Circle (JVC) consistently delivers the highest gross yields in Dubai at 8–9% for apartments in 2025. International City, Deira, and Dubai South also achieve 7–8%. These areas benefit from high tenant demand and relatively affordable property prices.

What is the difference between gross and net rental yield?

Gross yield = annual rental income ÷ property value. Net yield deducts annual costs: service charges (AED 12–32/sqft depending on community), property management fees (5–10% of rent), and a vacancy allowance (typically 5–8%). Net yields in Dubai average 1.5–2% below gross.

Is Dubai rental income taxable?

No. Dubai and the UAE impose no personal income tax on rental income for individuals. There is also no capital gains tax on property sales. This makes the gross yield comparison with other markets even more favourable, as yields in London and New York are taxed at 20–40%.

How do I calculate rental yield in Dubai?

Gross Yield (%) = (Annual Rent ÷ Property Price) × 100. Example: AED 72,000 annual rent on a AED 900,000 JVC apartment = 8.0% gross yield. Net yield deducts service charges (~AED 12,000/yr for JVC), management fees (~AED 5,760/yr at 8%), giving ~6.0% net yield.
